 Follow Us On: News SCIENCE Delhi-NCR temperatures to drop, Cyclone Akvan to intensify on Wednesday Delhi-NCR temperatures to drop, Cyclone Akvan to intensify on Wednesday
 Delhi may record minimum temperatures of 12–14°C on November 18 as Cyclone Akvan strengthens and approaches the Andhra Pradesh coast.
 Advertisement The IMD has issued an orange cyclone alert for the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts. (Photo: AP) By: India Today Science Desk New Delhi , Nov 17, 2026 19:30 IST Last Updated Nov 17, 2026 19:30 IST Published by Aryan Nov 17, 2026 19:30 IST Cyclone Akvan is expected to strengthen further over the Bay of Bengal on Wednesday, November 18, as it moves towards the Andhra Pradesh coast .
 The India Meteorological Department ( IMD ) has also forecast rain and thunderstorms in parts of southern and eastern India.
 In Delhi -NCR, temperatures are set to dip further, bringing a noticeable winter chill. The capital is likely to see a mainly clear sky, with mist or shallow fog in the morning. 
 High waves crash against the shoreline as rough sea conditions prevail ahead of Cyclone Akvan . (Photo: PTI) 
 advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story CYCLONE AKVAN GAINS STRENGTH
 Already a cyclonic storm on November 17, Akvan is expected to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by Tuesday evening and further strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm by the morning of November 19.
 It is forecast to move northwestwards and cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni around noon on November 20. At landfall, it could pack sustained winds of 120-130 kmph, gusting to 145 kmph.
 On November 18, isolated heavy rain is likely over Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam. Rayalaseema may also receive showers, while thundersqualls along the coast could bring winds of 60-70 kmph, gusting to 80 kmph. 
 A satellite image shows Cyclone Akvan brewing in the Bay of Bengal. (Photo: IMD) 
 Heavy to very heavy rain, with extremely heavy falls at isolated places, is forecast over Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam on November 19 and 20. Telangana is likely to receive heavy rain on November 20 and 21.
 The IMD has forecast fairly widespread rain over the Andaman and Nicobar Islands on November 18.
 Odisha may see isolated heavy rain and thunderstorms, with gusty winds of 40-50 kmph, gusting to 60 kmph. Chhattisgarh may receive isolated rain on November 18 and 19.
 No significant weather is expected over western and northeastern India during the week. 
 Vehicles move through dense fog on a cold morning. (Photo: PTI) 
 DELHI-NCR TO GET COLDER
 Delhi is likely to record a maximum temperature of 25-27°C and a minimum of 12-14°C on November 18, with day temperatures below normal at most places.
 The maximum is expected to fall to 24-26°C on November 19 and 20, while minimum temperatures may settle at 11-13°C.
 The gradual dip, alongside cooler mornings and fog, signals winter becoming more noticeable across the capital region. 
 Dense fog is also very likely in isolated pockets of east and west Uttar Pradesh on November 18. - Ends
